text:
The Islanders ended a four-game winless run (0-2-2) in the least likely way, beating a Kings team that controlled most of the game. Ilya Sorokin, drafted 78th overall in 2014 and a star at CSKA Moskva before he came over, made 26 saves on 28 shots, and by our numbers he stopped about one goal more than the chances against him should have allowed. That mattered, because NYI won 5-2 in a game LAK deserved to win about 80 percent of the time.

"Deserved to win" is the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, and the replays favored Los Angeles heavily. The Kings put up 69 shot attempts to 37, and they out-chanced the Islanders 3.18 to 2.02 in expected goals, a measure of shot quality. The second period was the clearest gap, 1.58 to 0.48. Yet Matthew Schaefer scored on a power play on a 4 percent chance, and Victor Eklund made it 3-1 early in the second. Darcy Kuemper allowed 2.5 goals more than the 20 shots he faced deserved, which turned a lopsided game into a comfortable one for New York.

Brayden Schenn, the Kings' fifth overall pick in 2009, picked up a goal and two assists against his old club. Simon Holmstrom added a goal and an assist, and Bo Horvat sealed it late. For the Islanders, it ends the winless stretch and avenges an overtime loss to LAK on Oct. 22. Los Angeles, for all its territorial edge, has to wonder what more it could have done.
